video.title: This Little AI Device Will Print Millionaires

summary: Chris Koerner and Nick discuss ways to build AI implementation services around a voice-recording pendant, especially for physicians and sales teams. They brainstorm other uses in assisted living, therapy, retail, remote work and coaching, while noting that integrations, consent and privacy create real barriers. The conversation also explores AI-powered background research and a possible pay-per-use Deep Research website. Most of the business ideas are hypotheses rather than tested operations.

acquisition_channels.details: The guest found an opening by talking with his bishop and the bishop's wife about the clinic's work.

tactics.name: Pilot the physician workflow with loaner devices
steps: Buy a small set of devices and approach a physician or clinic in person.
Offer a short trial and explain what is recorded, where it is stored and how to turn it off.
Show the physician a sample summary, then map any approved note workflow to the clinic's systems.
Confirm privacy, consent and EHR constraints before promising automated record updates.

quote.text: wear it for two days and then I'm going to show you what it does and if you like it, we can implement it

tactics.name: Start with a workflow the customer already understands
steps: Target businesses that already use scribes or routinely capture conversations.
Position the device as a way to improve an existing process rather than asking staff to invent a new one.
Begin with a summary or transcript before attempting deeper software integration.
Expand into structured record updates only after the first workflow is accepted.

tactics.name: Turn field sales recordings into repeatable coaching
steps: Get the sales manager's approval and explain the recording indicator and controls to staff.
Collect recordings and transcripts from the team.
Ask AI to identify strong interactions and quote specific examples verbatim.
Use the examples in the next team meeting and let a manager verify recommendations.

quote.text: I want you to pull out the five things he did best, like specific conversations, word for word, verbatim.

tactics.name: Test a pay-per-use research price
steps: Offer an occasional-use option for customers who do not need a monthly plan.
Compare a $1 prompt price with the stated estimated API cost of 30 to 50 cents.
Measure actual usage, processing costs, payment fees and support before offering unlimited plans.

quote.text: And my cost on that based on token usage would be 30 to 50 cents. So not like a huge margin, but that's fine.

tactics.name: Use deep research to locate hard-to-find business owners
steps: Start with the facts the buyer knows about the person or target business.
Ask the research tool to identify public records and related businesses.
Cross-check names and details against primary public records before making contact.
Use the result to guide the buyer's own outreach and due diligence.
